item.title: Kansas governor’s legislative priorities in 2026 center on budget, water and children
item.description: Gov. Laura Kelly said developing a budget would be her primary quest for 2026. Other priorities center on water resources and early childhood programs. Continue reading ...

item.title: Sheryl Sanders, champion of stable housing, retires from the Lawrence Community Shelter
item.description: Social work is woven into Sheryl Sanders as much as she’s woven into Lawrence. Sanders has retired as one of the longest-tenured Lawrence Community Shelter employees. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence Public Library dares patrons to be curious with new January reading challenge
item.description: The new year at the Lawrence Public Library will kick off not with a bang, but with a dare that encourages patrons to confront the post-holiday winter doldrums with a reading challenge. Continue reading ...

item.title: Kaw Valley Almanac for Dec. 29, 2025 – Jan. 4, 2026
item.description: Look closely: all those little black dots in the beautiful blue sky are robins. They are a fairly common in Kansas winters, with hundreds or even thousands in a flock. Continue reading ...

item.title: Kansan returns to the Catholic Church as the state’s first woman priest
item.description: Tina Thompson found a different way to be Catholic. She said she is the first Roman Catholic Woman Priest in Kansas, but she is one of hundreds of women Catholic priests around the world. Continue reading ...

item.title: Applications for Lawrence’s community arts grants open Wednesday
item.description: The City of Lawrence will soon welcome arts grant applications for projects with community value, including work focused on equity and inclusion and sustainability. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence police issue silver alert for missing man, 77
item.description: Lawrence police are asking for the public's help to locate Roger Harry Bean, 77. Continue reading ...

item.title: Here’s how to apply to access Lawrence’s rec centers for free
item.description: The City of Lawrence will start charging fees for adults to use recreation centers effective next Monday, but people who have already qualified for certain benefits can now apply for free access. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence community members can ask questions about planned fire station during upcoming session
item.description: A public engagement event hosted by the city will allow residents to speak with the project team that's planning the new fire station that's coming to Sixth and Stoneridge. Continue reading ...
